Register a Network Estimator

Source: R/estimator_registry.R
register_estimator.Rd

register_estimator() adds an estimator function to the registry that build_network() reads, so that build_network(data, method = name) calls it the way it calls a built-in method; the package registers its fourteen built-in methods with this function when it loads. A name already in the registry is replaced, built-ins included, without a message. list_estimators() shows what is registered and remove_estimator() takes an entry out.

A name that build_network() maps to a different built-in method (an alias such as "tna" or "ebicglasso") is resolved to that method before the registry is read, so an estimator registered under it is never called; pick a name that is not an alias.

Usage

register_estimator(name, fn, description, directed)

Arguments

name

The name the estimator is called by, as method in build_network(): a single non-empty string. A name already registered is replaced.

fn

The estimator function. Its first argument is data, and it must accept ..., because build_network() passes every setting by name. It returns a list with matrix (the square numeric weight matrix), nodes (the node names, in the matrix's order) and directed (TRUE or FALSE); see Details for the optional elements.

description

A short description of the estimator, a single string, shown by list_estimators().

directed

Whether the estimator produces directed networks, TRUE or FALSE. build_network() reads it to decide whether level (the multilevel decomposition) is allowed: a directed estimator refuses it. The edges of the network follow the directed element fn returns, but bootstrap_network() reads this registered flag to build its edge tables, so the two should agree.

Value

NULL, invisibly. The estimator is added to the registry as a side effect.

Details

build_network() calls the function as fn(data = data, ...), where ... holds the params list, the further arguments given to build_network() and a format setting, which is why fn must accept .... When actor names a column of wide or association data (long data is prepared by build_network() itself) and fn has an id_col argument (or, failing that and for data that is not one-hot, an id argument), the actor column is passed under that name unless params already sets it. Scaling, thresholding and the edge list are then applied to the returned matrix, as for a built-in method.

Besides matrix, nodes and directed, the returned list may hold cleaned_data, the data frame the network was estimated from, which build_network() splits into the network's data and metadata fields; any other named element is copied onto the netobject, replacing a field of the same name. A return value without matrix, nodes or directed makes build_network() stop with an error.

See also

get_estimator, list_estimators, remove_estimator, build_network

Examples

my_fn <- function(data, ...) {
  m <- cor(data)
  diag(m) <- 0
  list(matrix = m, nodes = colnames(m), directed = FALSE)
}
register_estimator("my_cor", my_fn, "Custom correlation", directed = FALSE)
df <- data.frame(A = rnorm(20), B = rnorm(20), C = rnorm(20))
net <- build_network(df, method = "my_cor")
remove_estimator("my_cor")
